corrected_json.statement_latex:
Let a dynamical system $\dot{\boldsymbol z}=\boldsymbol f(\boldsymbol z)$ be given in $\mathbb R^m$ with flow map $\mathscr F_t:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^m$ which we assume to be continuously differentiable. Let $\boldsymbol z(t,\boldsymbol\zeta)$ represent the solution of initial value problem
\[\dot{\boldsymbol z}=\boldsymbol f(\boldsymbol z),\qquad\boldsymbol z(0)=\boldsymbol\zeta.\]
We then compute the $m\times m$ Jacobian matrix of $\mathscr F_t(\boldsymbol z(t,\boldsymbol\zeta))$:
\[\boldsymbol W(t)=\mathscr F_t'(\boldsymbol z(t,\boldsymbol\zeta))=\frac{\partial\mathscr F_t}{\partial\boldsymbol z}(\boldsymbol z(t,\boldsymbol\zeta)).\]
